$comment: The case table for text-quote resolution (frontend/anchor.js findQuoteIndex),
kept as data rather than inline so the cases are readable as a spec and can be
added to without touching test plumbing.
Offsets are UTF-16 code units, because that is what JS string indices are and
the context window is a fixed count of them. Half these cases exist to pin
that: an implementation counting bytes or code points agrees on ASCII and
diverges on the first emoji, where one character is two code units.
`index` absent means the quote does not resolve at all — the caller renders
that as drifted. Every field here is asserted; `$note` is prose for the
reader, and is the only thing that isn't.
Two cases can't live in JSON and stay hand-written in anchor.test.js: a prefix
beginning on an unpaired surrogate (JSON cannot carry a lone surrogate), and
anything asserting that a call terminates rather than hangs.

cases.name: unique quote — context is redundant but must not break the match
unique quote with no context at all
duplicate quotes — prefix disambiguates to the second
cases.text: the cat sat. the dog sat. done

cases.name: duplicate quotes — suffix disambiguates to the second
cases.text: x: value one. x: value two.

cases.name: duplicate quotes — prefix+suffix together pick the middle one
cases.text: a ref b. c ref d. e ref f.

cases.name: duplicate quotes — no occurrence agrees, so the first wins (known-wrong)
cases.$note: The expected offset here is the WRONG one, deliberately. When the text around a quote has been edited so no occurrence matches the recorded context, the scan falls through and returns the first hit — very likely a different paragraph than the reviewer selected. Reporting drift on text that is plainly still present tested worse. If this case changes, someone revisited that trade-off on purpose.
cases.text: one HIT two HIT three HIT four

cases.name: the same haystack with context that does agree picks the third
cases.text: one HIT two HIT three HIT four

cases.name: empty prefix opts out of the prefix check; suffix still decides
cases.$note: A selection at the very start of a document legitimately records prefix ''. Empty is falsy, so it disables that half of disambiguation — the same path as 'no prefix recorded'.

cases.name: absent prefix behaves exactly like an empty one
cases.$note: The daemon omits absent context via skip_serializing_if, so selectors arrive with the field missing rather than empty. Both must behave identically.

cases.name: a quote at the very start has no prefix to check
a quote at the very end has no suffix to check
prefix longer than the 32-unit window matches on its tail
cases.$note: Only the last 32 units are compared, because that is all captureSelector recorded and all the haystack slice provides.

cases.name: suffix longer than the 32-unit window matches on its head
no match — quote is simply gone
a quote longer than the haystack is absent, not an error
an empty haystack has nothing to find
an empty quote is unanchorable
cases.$note: Also load-bearing for termination — see the hand-written companion case. indexOf('', n) clamps to length instead of returning -1, so an unguarded scan whose cursor is found+1 stops advancing the result and loops until the tab dies.

cases.name: an empty quote with no context either
cases.$note: A behaviour change, not just a hang fix. Without the guard this case did NOT hang — with no context to disagree with, the first iteration matched and returned 0, i.e. a zero-length highlight at the start of the document. It now reports no match and renders as drifted, which is the honest answer for a quote that cannot be anchored to anything.

cases.name: combining marks are matched as written, never normalized
cases.$note: 'e' + U+0301 is two code units and is not equal to precomposed U+00E9. No normalization happens anywhere, so a selector recorded in one form will not match text stored in the other. Asserted so the limitation is documented rather than discovered by a reviewer whose comment vanished.

cases.name: precomposed matches precomposed
emoji before the quote shift the offset by two units each
cases.$note: Three astral characters = 6 code units, so TARGET starts at 6 + ' aim at '.length.

cases.name: an astral prefix filling the window exactly still matches
cases.$note: 16 emoji = 32 code units, the whole window.

cases.name: self-overlapping quote — the scan steps one unit, not the match length
cases.$note: Occurrence 2 begins inside occurrence 1. A cursor advancing by the match length skips it and answers 2 instead of 1. This is the only shape that observes the step size, and randomly generated text does not reliably produce it.

cases.name: self-overlapping, longer quote
self-overlapping with a repeating multi-unit token
self-overlapping, disambiguated by suffix instead
self-overlapping astral quote
